title: NOT TO BE TREATED AS A SLAVE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If any of your fellow Israelites become poor and sell themselves to you,
do not make them work as slaves. They are to be treated as hired workers or
temporary residents among you; they are to work for you until the Year of
Jubilee'" - Lev 25:39-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When crushing poverty forced an Israelite to sell his labour to a fellow
Israelite, God set firm limits. Such a person was not to be treated as a
slave but as a hired worker — with dignity — and the arrangement had an end
point at the Jubilee. Poverty could not be turned into permanent bondage.

We should read this honestly. This was regulation within an ancient economy
where the desperately poor sometimes had no option but to sell their labour.
God did not endorse treating people as property; He constrained it, dignified
the worker, and guaranteed an exit.

Dear friend, the direction of God's law is always toward the dignity of
persons. A human being made in God's image was never to be reduced to a mere
possession, no matter how poor they became. There was always a limit, always
an appointed release.

The New Testament carries this direction further. Paul told masters to treat
their servants justly, remembering that they too have a Master in heaven
(Col 4:1). He urged Philemon to receive his returning servant Onesimus no
longer as a slave but as a beloved brother (Philem 15-16). The gospel dignifies
every person.

Whoever works for you or under you — an employee, a helper, a junior — bears
God's image and answers to the same Master you do. Treat them accordingly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat those who work for me with full dignity?
2. Is there anyone under my authority I have treated as less than a person?
3. How does remembering my own Master in heaven shape how I lead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me treat everyone who works with me or for me with dignity, as
those who bear Your image. Remind me that I too serve a Master in heaven.
Amen.
